technique: Best read from the keyframes is rigged 3D CGI made to *look* like stop-motion/claymation rather than actual physical stop-motion: skin has a glossy, slightly waxy clay-like specular highlight, the woman's sweater uses a felted/fuzzy fiber shader, and both characters have exaggerated, asymmetric caricature proportions (long hooked noses, small deep-set eyes) reminiscent of Aardman-style puppets. Against that, there is zero set jitter, no fingerprint/tool-mark texture, no lighting flicker, and the static-camera frames line up pixel-perfectly on background geometry (dresser, painting, lamp, curtains) across all periodic samples -- all of which argue against true frame-by-frame photographed puppetry and for a digital render with a stop-motion-emulating art style. Confidence is moderate; without in-between (non-keyframe) frames it's not possible to confirm whether poses are interpolated continuously or held/stepped like classic 2s-on-2s stop-motion timing.
facial_animation_notes: Mouth shapes change per spoken word/viseme across the sampled frames (e.g., open round shape on "DON'T", narrower shape on "ANYMORE", neutral on "WE", wide gap-toothed open-mouth shock on "WHAT?", then a smirking closed grin on "ACID REFLUX"), consistent with rig-driven lip sync rather than a small fixed set of held mouth poses. The man's face shows a recurring sly asymmetric smirk with visible upper teeth and an eyebrow raise that appears to build gradually rather than snap between two states. The woman's face moves from a flat/tired expression in early frames to progressively raised eyebrows, widened eyes, and an open-mouthed shocked grin by periodic-6/7, again reading as smooth build rather than a hard cut between poses.
eye_and_blink_notes: No blink was caught in any of the 11 periodic samples (~1s apart), so blink timing/frequency cannot be characterized from this data -- flagged as a sampling limitation rather than an animation absence. Eye direction does shift meaningfully between frames: the woman's gaze tracks up and to the side (periodic-2, periodic-4) as if reacting to the man off to her left, and the man's eyes are cast down toward the clothes he's folding in the early/mid frames before lifting to meet her gaze later. Eyes have a glossy CG specular dot typical of rendered (not painted) eyeballs.
head_movement_notes: The woman's head tilts back and her chin lifts progressively across periodic-4 through periodic-7, consistent with a building physical reaction (surprise/indignation) rather than a single static pose. The man's head is mostly angled downward toward the folded clothes/chair in early-to-mid frames and rotates slightly upward and toward the woman in later frames; the change in his head angle across frames is gradual, not an abrupt snap, again suggesting interpolated rather than heavily-held animation. No frame shows a head pose repeated identically, which argues against long multi-frame holds at this sampling interval.
gesture_notes: The man performs a continuous small-object-handling gesture across the sequence -- holding/adjusting a stack of folded dark clothing/towels against a chair, with his arm and hand position shifting incrementally frame to frame (periodic-1 through periodic-7) rather than staying locked, indicating a genuine animated action rather than a static prop hold. In the opening/title frames he holds a phone up near his face. The woman keeps her hands clasped together at chest height for nearly the entire sampled range, with only small finger/wrist adjustments (a ring is visible and catches light differently across frames), reading as a restrained, tense idle gesture rather than active gesturing.
idle_motion_notes: The set is largely inert between character performances: the ceiling fan blades are in the same static position in every sampled frame (no rotation), the curtains show no fabric movement, and the lamp, glass, phone-charging cable, and books on the nightstand/bed are pixel-identical in position across frames. The only ambient motion visible is the city-light glow through the window, which stays constant in brightness/pattern. This suggests idle/secondary animation is concentrated entirely on the two characters, with the environment held essentially static.
frame_rate_feel: Metadata reports 30fps for an ~11-second clip. Across the periodic keyframes (~1s apart), poses and expressions never repeat identically and appear to progress incrementally rather than jumping between a small number of held extremes, which reads as animation close to full/smooth interpolation rather than an obvious 2s/12fps stutter-hold style. However, the periodic sampling interval is too coarse to rule out short holds or stepped rotation within a given second, so this read should be treated as an approximation, not a frame-accurate measurement.
overall_animation_style_notes: The overall look is a single locked-off wide shot of a bedroom scene, character-acting-driven comedy (a couple mid-argument while packing/folding clothes), rendered in a caricatured, big-nosed, clay/felt-textured 3D style that visually quotes stop-motion studios (Aardman/Laika) without the physical-camera artifacts of actual stop-motion. Expression changes (eyebrows, mouth, head tilt) are the primary storytelling tool, matched tightly to the on-screen caption words ("DON'T", "ANYMORE", "WE", "WHAT?", "ACID REFLUX"), and the environment is kept deliberately static so that all visual attention lands on the two performing characters.
